activity.notes: ATLAS uses c.1350 CE only as a representative historical activity point associated with Ñancempinco's first phase of Chimú expansion; it is not asserted as an accession year, death year, or full reign span. Ethnohistoric and archaeological scholarship considers a historical king of this name plausible, while also warning that the later dynastic tradition compresses chronology.

sources.title: Farfan, General Pacatnamu, And The Dynastic History Of Chimor — eHRAF Archaeology
sources.citation_text: The eHRAF summary states that archaeology seems to confirm the historical reality of the Chimú conquest and perhaps of a king called Ñançenpinco, while warning that the traditional dynastic chronology is not fully accurate.

sources.title: Chimú — Encyclopedia.com
sources.citation_text: The reference places Ñançenpinco's first phase of imperial expansion around 1350 CE and associates his conquests with the Jequetepeque and Santa valleys.
